name: Brandy Library
address: 25 N Moore St, New York, NY 10013
take: Leather chairs, a fifteen-page spirits list, and a room that stays quiet on purpose; the place for one slow, expensive drink you'll remember.
theCatch: Book ahead, parties of six max, nobody under 25, and it's closed on Sundays.
notes: Spirits lounge on N Moore between Varick and West Broadway with a 1,500-plus bottle inventory and backlit stave walls. Open 4pm-midnight Mon-Wed, 4pm-2am Thu-Sat, closed Sunday; reservations via Tock, walk-ins by phone; over-25 policy; small bar-food menu. VIP room and lower-level lounge for private groups.

name: Nancy Whiskey Pub
take: A 1967 dive with a shuffleboard table, cheap pints, and a 4am license; the last stop in a neighborhood that mostly goes to bed early.
theCatch: Kitchen runs till 3am; the shuffleboard table is the seat you want, so claim it early.
notes: Two-floor dive at Lispenard and West Broadway, a block below Canal, open since 1967. Hours 11am-4am Mon-Sat, noon-4am Sun, kitchen till 3am. Shuffleboard, jukebox, burgers, wings and fried bar snacks; the latest license in the neighborhood.

name: Puffy's Tavern
take: A 1940s corner bar where the regulars know the bartender, the game is on, and the Italian sandwiches are better than they need to be.
theCatch: The Alidoro sandwiches only run noon to five, and on Sundays the whole place shuts at 8.
notes: Small 1940s-era pub at Hudson and Harrison. Open 11:30am-1am Mon, till 2am Tue-Thu, 3am Fri, noon-3am Sat, noon-8pm Sun. TVs for games, a dart lane, happy hour, and Italian sandwiches from Alidoro served midday; a regulars' bar with light beer and well drinks.

name: Saint Tuesday
take: Ring a bell in an alley, take a narrow back staircase, and there's a jazz trio playing to a sub-cellar of booths built for two.
theCatch: Live music Tuesday through Saturday only and cocktails run $22; reserve on Resy if you want a booth.
notes: Basement bar of the Walker Hotel Tribeca (77 Walker St), entered from Cortlandt Alley; the building sits a few steps east of Broadway but is run and marketed as a Tribeca bar. Jazz Tue-Wed 8:30-11pm and Thu-Sat 9pm-12:30am, no cover; cocktails $22-24, wine $16-22, beer $9, small bites; reservations on Resy.

name: WarrenPeace
take: The old Warren 77 sports bar with the TVs pulled out and candles put in: a dim corner room for a long drink and a dinner nobody planned.
theCatch: Closed Sundays and done by midnight most nights; order the duck-fat parm fries whatever else you do.
notes: Corner of Warren and West Broadway, one block below Chambers, in the former Warren 77 space; opened 2022 by Briken Fejzullai, who kept the reverse-L bar and opaque windows and removed the screens. Mon-Thu 4pm-midnight, Fri-Sat till 1am, closed Sunday. Mediterranean and Balkan sharing plates, classic cocktails, wine and beer; Resy reservations.

name: Macao Trading Co.
take: Chinese-Portuguese plates upstairs, a cushioned lounge with DJs downstairs, and a 4am close on weekends; the one Tribeca room that actually goes late.
theCatch: Dress code bans caps and athletic gear; the late menu starts at midnight and the basement is where the night is.
notes: Multi-level bar-restaurant on Church between Walker and Lispenard: harp-shaped bar and dining room upstairs, a cushion-seated lounge with a second bar downstairs. Sun-Mon 5pm-midnight, Tue-Wed till 2am, Thu-Sat till 4am with DJs and dancing; late-night menu after midnight; proper-dress policy (no caps, jerseys, workout clothes). Happy hour Sun-Thu 5-7pm with $2 oysters; reservations through the website.

name: Mudville 9
take: A wings-and-beer sports bar that has been on Chambers since 1977 and behaves like it: more screens than tables, and nobody dressed up.
theCatch: Knicks and NFL nights fill every stool; get there before tip-off or plan on standing at the bar.
notes: Chambers between West Broadway and Church, a neighborhood sports bar since 1977 with 25-plus taps and TVs at nearly every table. Site lists 11:30am-11pm Sun-Mon and 11:30am-1am Tue-Sat; happy hour Mon-Fri 3-6pm; wings, burgers, ribs, pizza. One Yelp listing shows it as closed, but the venue's own site and two 2026 directories show it operating; worth a phone check before sending a big group.

name: Terroir Tribeca
take: Paul Grieco's wine bar takes wine seriously and itself not at all: a huge by-the-glass list, meatball sandwiches, and an after-work crowd that stays.
theCatch: Loud with the office crowd until about 8 on weeknights; weekends are calmer and more local.
notes: Harrison between Greenwich and Hudson; from sommelier Paul Grieco and Marco Canora. Opens 4pm daily, reservations via the website. Mediterranean-leaning bar food (meatball sandwich, oxtail risotto balls, bone-marrow bruschetta), a long wine list with a deep by-the-glass section, a few beer taps, oysters at happy hour. Corporate crowd early on weeknights, neighborhood crowd on weekends.

name: Little More
take: A newish neighborhood bar with a neon BAR sign, purse hooks, a long cocktail list, and a bookshelf door to a Wednesday-only speakeasy downstairs.
theCatch: The basement room is Wednesdays only, by email reservation with a two-drink minimum; upstairs walks in, happy hour noon to six.
notes: Reade between West Broadway and Church, in the former Ward III space; opened November 2024 by Aron Watman (The Folly). Beer on tap, long cocktail list, wine from $11, happy hour noon-6pm. Hidden basement bar behind a bookshelf runs Wednesdays 7pm-1am, reservations via info@littlemorenyc.com, capacity about 40, also bookable for private parties.

name: Grand Banks
address: Pier 25, 225 West St, New York, NY 10013
take: Oysters and rosé on the deck of a wooden schooner at Pier 25, with the Hudson going orange behind you; the neighborhood's only real outdoor bar.
theCatch: Seasonal: it reopened mid-April and closes for winter, so check first; book on SevenRooms and bring a layer.
notes: Oyster bar aboard the Sherman Zwicker, a historic wooden schooner docked at Pier 25 in Hudson River Park off N Moore St; seasonal, 2026 season opened April 13. Mon-Fri 11am-midnight, weekends brunch from 9am then service till midnight; reservations for up to 10 via SevenRooms. Oysters, small plates by chef Kerry Heffernan, cocktails, Champagne, beer. Sits on the water, so weather decides the night.

name: The Django
address: 2 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10013
take: A vaulted-brick cellar under the Roxy Hotel with live jazz seven nights, two bars, and dinner; it's a club with a cover, and worth it.
theCatch: Cover is $35-40 plus a two-drink minimum, and no-shows get charged; book a set on Resy and arrive early.
notes: Cellar level of the Roxy Hotel at Sixth Ave and Canal/White, styled after Parisian jazz caves with exposed brick and vaulted ceilings. Jazz nightly, doors Mon-Sat 6:30pm and Sun 6pm; cover $35 Sun-Thu, $40 Fri-Sat, two-drink minimum, 24-hour cancellation. Cocktails $15-24, small plates $18-28, entrees to $54, late-night menu after 11pm; Resy, groups of five-plus by phone. Monday is a next-gen showcase, Tuesday is Latin night.

name: Primo's
take: Red-jacketed bartenders, conch-shell lamps, and $22 martinis up front; later on a back room opens with a DJ and people actually dance.
theCatch: Closed Sunday and Monday, midnight close Tuesday and Wednesday; the back room is a Thursday-to-Saturday thing.
notes: Lobby bar of the Frederick Hotel on Chambers between West Broadway and Church, opened 2018 by the Mr. Fong's and Oliver Coffee partners; velvet seating and a 1920s throwback look, with a separate back room that turns into a DJ dance floor. Tue-Wed 4pm-midnight, Thu-Fri 4pm-2am, Sat 5pm-2am, closed Sun-Mon; Resy for tables, private party room available.

name: The Hideaway
take: Twenty years on Duane Park with the same cooks and the same regulars: a bar with TVs, a good burger, and blue crabs when it's summer.
theCatch: Thursday and Saturday nights are the ones the regulars pick; blue crab night is seasonal, so ask before you plan on it.
notes: Duane between Greenwich and Staple, facing Duane Park; opened early 2006 by a group of Chesapeake Bay finance people as a nod to a Duke bar of the same name. Listed hours noon-midnight daily. Exposed brick, black-and-white photos, TVs; burgers, wings, quesadilla, crab cakes, Maryland blue crabs in season. The Seaport branch closed in 2024, leaving this as the only one.

name: Locanda Verde
take: Carmellini's Italian taverna in the Greenwich Hotel: sheep's-milk ricotta, a big room that fits every kind of table, and a bar worth eating at alone.
theCatch: Reservations are easy for once; the bar takes walk-ins, and dinner ends at 10 early in the week.
notes: Greenwich at N Moore, in the Greenwich Hotel; Andrew Carmellini's Italian, running since 2009. Dinner Sun-Wed 5-10pm, Thu-Sat 5-11pm; also breakfast, lunch and weekend brunch. Online reservations for up to 8, full bar with walk-in seats, big round tables for groups. Ricotta crostini, lamb meatball sliders and the ravioli are the standards.

name: Chambers
take: A 63-seat wine restaurant where sommeliers eat on their night off: twenty pours by the glass, a marble bar for walk-ins, and a kitchen that keeps up.
theCatch: Tuesday to Saturday from 6 only; grab the marble bar, or the communal table, which opens to walk-ins after 6:45.
notes: Chambers between Church and Broadway, in the former Racines NY space; partners include David Lillie of Chambers Street Wines and sommelier Pascaline Lepeltier, chef Jonathan Karis. Open Tue-Sat from 6pm; OpenTable, plus walk-ins at the 21-seat kitchen-facing bar and the front communal table. James Beard finalist; wines by the glass from about $10 draft pours to a $49 aged savagnin; menu changes often, sesame bread and the lamb are the fixtures.

name: Paros
take: Greek with fine-dining manners on a bright corner at Franklin and West Broadway; the bar by the windows fills first and stays full.
theCatch: Kitchen closes at 10, so it's the first half of the night; happy hour from 3:30 is the cheap way in.
notes: Northeast corner of West Broadway and Franklin, opened March 2024 by brothers George (chef, a Top Chef finalist) and Nick Pagonis in a high-ceilinged, light-filled room with a bar over the street. Open daily 11:30am-10pm; happy hour 3:30-6pm with $10 wine and oysters. Dips, halloumi with honey, grilled octopus, tuna tartare around $28; Greek wines and good cocktails.

name: Estancia 460
take: Argentine-Italian canteen at the top of Greenwich Street that locals treat as their clubhouse: milanesa, empanadas, a jalapeño-tequila Rosalita, no fuss.
theCatch: Happy hour runs noon to 7 on weekdays, and the sidewalk seats go early on warm nights.
notes: Greenwich between Watts and Desbrosses near the Canal Street edge; Argentine with Italian and Spanish leanings, open since 1995, owner Stacey Sosa. About 80 percent local crowd. Weekday happy hour noon-7pm; sidewalk seating; Resy reservations and private events. Chicken milanese is the top seller; South American wine list and the house Rosalita cocktail.

name: Faux
take: Keith McNally's son's first restaurant: a French coastal brasserie on Church with a vaulted bar underneath that runs late; brand new and already hard to book.
theCatch: The downstairs bar is Tuesday to Saturday only; upstairs runs daily 5pm to midnight and takes walk-ins if you're flexible.
notes: Church between Franklin and White, in the former B Flat and Shigure space; opened September 2026 by George McNally (Keith McNally's son) with chef Kristina Ramos, ex-L'Abeille. Two floors: ground-floor brasserie open daily 5pm-midnight, vaulted downstairs bar Tue-Sat; OpenTable with walk-ins welcome; $50-plus per person. Furniture and design borrowed from the McNally playbook. Very new, so early impressions only.
